item.title: Fire breaks out at Albania's Education Ministry during student protest
item.description: Albania's Education Ministry caught fire on Wednesday during a second day of student protests over corruption and education, as police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds in Tirana.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Albania's Education Ministry caught fire on Wednesday during a second day of student protests over corruption and education, as police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds in Tirana. Thousands of protesters gathered in front of the Education Ministry on Wednesday. Some threw bricks at the building. They broke metal sidewalk barriers and overturned trash cans, Reuters footage showed. A Raiffeisen Bank branch nearby caught fire as well, a Reuters witness said. This has been the most violent outburst of anti-corruption protests, which started in May and have posed a growing challenge to Prime Minister Edi Rama's government. "Protesting is a legitimate right, but it cannot be used as an excuse for violence, city destruction or ugly fighting in the middle of the road," Deputy Prime Minister Albana Kociu said on Facebook. "I call on students and every honest citizen who believes in the right to protest: Distance yourself from violence and vandalism!" Student organisers said the protest was over conditions at universities, higher education costs, financial support and employment prospects after graduation. The unrest is part of a broader wave of student activism sweeping Europe over education and living conditions. In France, high school students have staged [USN:L1N45U08J TEXT:"weeks of protests"] and school blockades demanding more teachers and better facilities, arguing that deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded classrooms are undermining education.

item.title: EU Commission is in dialogue with Google, spokesperson says
item.description: The European Commission said on Wednesday it was "in dialogue with Google" over actions the company may take in response to the $1 billion fines imposed by the EU in July and required changes to its app store and its search engine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The European Commission said on Wednesday it was "in dialogue with Google" (GOOGL.O) over actions the company may take in response to the [USN:L1N43P0DE TEXT:"$1 billion fines"] imposed by the EU in July and required changes to its app store and its search engine. The Commission has fined Alphabet's Google €460 million ($511.43 million) and €430 million respectively for favouring its own services in shopping, hotels, transport and sports search results and for the restrictions for app developers on its app store Google Play. "We are currently in dialogue with Google, so I'll not prejudge the outcome of this dialogue, but I can guarantee you that the Commission services are currently in dialogue with Google precisely on this issue," spokesperson Thomas Regnier said during a daily EU press briefing. The Commission ordered Google to comply with recommendations to treat rivals in a fair and non-discriminatory manner and allow app developers to steer users away from its app store within 60 days. The Commission is aware that Google has already started implementing changes to its search engine results and has announced and implemented some changes to the service fees for app developers on Google Play, the spokesperson's office said in a statement. "The Commission will carry out a thorough assessment of the measures. As part of this assessment, the Commission will seek the views of market operators and third parties," the statement said. ($1 = 0.8994 euros)

item.title: Mexico to require digital platforms to protect minors from violent, sexual content
item.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said she will sign a presidential decree later on Wednesday requiring digital platforms, including social networks and streaming sites, to shield children and teenagers from violent, sexual and other harmful content.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said she will sign a presidential decree later on Wednesday requiring digital platforms, including social networks and streaming sites, to shield children and teenagers from violent, sexual and other harmful content. The decree, which will step up scrutiny of big technology companies in Latin America's second largest economy, comes after an [USN:L6N45N12T TEXT:"attack by two 18-year-old former students on a high school"] in the northern state of Coahuila in early October left one person dead and wounded three others. Digital platforms will have one month to come into compliance with the decree, government adviser Luisa Maria Alcalde said. Sheinbaum added that if the decree was not followed by firms, the government would back a bill to levy punishments against platforms. Officials said they had already met with representatives of Meta (META.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Apple (AAPL.O) , TikTok, Google (GOOGL.O) , X and Huawei to discuss the matter. Mexico's move follows a broader [USN:L8N42Q0MC TEXT:"global push"] to protect minors online, with governments in Europe and Australia tightening oversight of digital platforms and US states pursuing a range of child-safety measures. [USN:S0N3S10A3 TEXT:"Brazil"] has also moved to strengthen protections for children online. Such measures have raised questions over how to protect minors while safeguarding privacy and freedom of expression.

item.title: Berkshire deepens Bending Spoons bet with $330 million, sparking share rally
item.description: Bending Spoons shares rallied 34% on Wednesday after Berkshire Hathaway invested another $330 million in the owner of Vimeo and AOL, a big endorsement from the high-profile investor whose moves traders closely follow.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bending Spoons (BSP.O) shares rallied 34% on Wednesday after Berkshire Hathaway (BRKa.N) invested another $330 million in the owner of Vimeo and AOL, a big endorsement from the high-profile investor whose moves traders closely follow. The purchase builds on the $600 million Berkshire invested in Bending Spoons' initial public offering in July. It lifts the Warren Buffett-founded conglomerate's stake in the company to 4%, making it Italian company's sixth-largest investor, according to LSEG data. Berkshire Hathaway, whose businesses span insurance, energy, rail transportation, manufacturing and retail, has a history of investing across industries. Under CEO Greg Abel, the conglomerate has [USN:L6N44U0RU TEXT:"increased"] its exposure to technology companies and AI, with Alphabet (GOOGL.O) becoming its third-largest common stock holding. Its largest stock investments include Apple (AAPL.O) . Bending Spoons will now issue 10 million ordinary shares to Berkshire at $33 per share. The company's stock, meanwhile, jumped to $51.10. Bending Spoons, which acquires and transforms struggling digital businesses, said the investment would strengthen its financial flexibility and support its acquisition strategy. It continues to evaluate merger and acquisition opportunities and has a strong pipeline, said Francesco Patarnello, co-founder and head of business acquisitions. Bending Spoons, which acquires and transforms digital businesses, has a portfolio that includes productivity software maker Airtable, pet-tracking company Tractive and file-sharing platform WeTransfer.

item.title: El ICSG prevé que el excedente mundial de cobre refinado aumente en 2027
item.description: El Grupo Internacional de Estudio del Cobre (ICSG, por su sigla en inglés) pronosticó el miércoles que el mercado mundial del cobre refinado se mantendría en superávit hasta 2027, y que dicho superávit pasaría de unas 104.000 toneladas métricas en 2026 a 368.000 toneladas métricas en 2027.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Grupo Internacional de Estudio del Cobre (ICSG, por su sigla en inglés) pronosticó el miércoles que el mercado mundial del cobre refinado se mantendría en superávit hasta 2027, y que dicho superávit pasaría de unas 104.000 toneladas métricas en 2026 a 368.000 toneladas métricas en 2027. El ICSG señaló que se prevé que la producción mundial de cobre refinado aumente en torno a un 0,4% en 2026 y un 3,4% en 2027. El grupo indicó que el incremento de la producción de cobre refinado el próximo año vendría impulsado por la puesta en marcha de fundiciones y refinerías en Indonesia, la India y la Unión Europea. Se espera que el consumo aparente de cobre refinado aumente en torno a un 1,5% en 2026 y un 2,5% en 2027. El grupo señaló que se espera que el consumo mundial de cobre siga viéndose respaldado por la mejora de la actividad manufacturera en algunos sectores clave de uso final del cobre, la demanda continuada derivada de la transición energética, la urbanización y la digitalización —incluidos los centros de datos y la inteligencia artificial— y el desarrollo de nueva capacidad de producción de semiconductores en varios países. Asia seguirá siendo el principal motor del crecimiento mundial, añadió. Se prevé que la producción mundial de las minas de cobre crezca un 1,3% en 2026 y un 3,1% en 2027, impulsada por la puesta en marcha de minas nuevas y ampliadas, así como por el aumento de la producción en los países productores.

Infantino faces FIFA rebels in Zurich after failed World Cup stake sale

FAST

ZURICH, Oct 14 : Gianni Infantino faces the soccer leaders who want him gone on Thursday in his first meeting with FIFA’s top brass since his plan to sell a stake in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup, collapsed. Infantino has faced calls to resign from the leaders of three regional football confederations – UEFA (Europe), AFC (Asia) and CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) – and their representatives will be present in Zurich for a FIFA Council meeting. They will be joined by their counterparts from Africa, South America and Oceania. On the agenda will be a discussion of the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, which Infantino was forced to abandon within days of announcing it in July.

Under the plan, Infantino proposed selling a minority stake in a FIFA commercial subsidiary to private investors, with a company launched by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, identified as the proposed lead investor. The 37-member council will also address FIFA’s governance, with some of the sport’s most powerful figures determined to limit Infantino’s powers if they cannot force him out of office. Infantino, 56, will stand for re-election in March 2027, with a November 18 deadline looming for potential candidates to submit their nominations. Last week, former. Switzerland and Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega announced that he intended to stand, but he has not confirmed whether he has the backing of the five national associations required to enter the race. The FFE plan exposed a split in world soccer, with Aleksander Ceferin, Salman Al Khalifa and Victor Montagliani - the presidents respectively of UEFA, AFC and CONCACAF - saying it was time for a change at the top of FIFA. However, Infantino has been canvassing support as he bids to remain in power and received a standing ovation when he met African soccer leaders last week in Cape Verde. He is also expected to be backed by South America at next year’s election in Rabat, Morocco. Despite the AFC’s criticism of his leadership, many countries within Asia, including a bloc of Arab nations, have offered their support. PEACE PRIZE People familiar with the matter told Reuters that although the chances of finding someone to replace Infantino were remote, his opponents were determined to leave him more isolated and curb his powers. In addition to reviewing FFE, council members are expected to discuss FIFA’s financial reserves and how much money it can release to member associations, as well as its disciplinary procedures, governance framework and Peace Prize, which was controversially awarded to U.S. President Donald Trump last year. Last month, UEFA and CONCACAF called on FIFA to release $10 million to each of its 211 member associations, countering Infantino’s FFE proposal under which associations could receive $20 million in development funding and potentially access a further $20 million. Emanuel Medeiros, founder and Global CEO of Sport Integrity Global Alliance, a pressure group for better governance in sport, said FIFA needed to have a “frank discussion” in Zurich. “The eyes of the world are on them,” he said. “The world of football expects to see a council that takes this unique opportunity to establish a genuinely independent, comprehensive and transparent governance review… We certainly wish to see a new impetus, a new dynamic.” However, lawyer and politician Miguel Maduro, who was chairman of the FIFA Governance Committee in 2016 before being sacked by Infantino, said he would be surprised if anything meaningful came of Thursday’s meeting. “They may announce the setting up of a Working Group or even an Independent Review of FIFA Governance but the credibility of either exercise will be very limited in the light of FIFA’s track record,” he said. “Such an exercise, if not genuinely independent and enforceable, might be more of the same: a window dressing exercise simply aimed at reducing public pressure and to state they have now addressed whatever problems they had.”

(Editing by Julien Pretot and Pritha Sarkar)

Source: Reuters

Oct 14 : Algerian winger Riyad Mahrez has joined Al Shamal on a free transfer after leaving Saudi Pro League side Al Ahli, the Qatar Stars League club announced on Wednesday. The 35-year-old, who announced his international retirement following this year's World Cup, departed Jeddah-based club Al Ahli after a decorated three-year stint. "His left foot made history and our ambition is writing the next chapter. Riyad Mahrez in Al Shamal colours," the Qatari club posted on X. Mahrez made his professional breakthrough at French side Le Havre before he joined Leicester City in 2014, where he became a central figure in the English club's fairytale Premier League triumph in 2016.

item.title: Wall Street cai após dados de inflação reforçarem apostas em alta dos juros nos EUA
item.description: Os principais índices de Wall Street registravam ligeira queda nesta quarta-feira, depois que um relatório de inflação dos EUA com dados acima do esperado reforçou apostas em um aumento da taxa de juros neste mês, enquanto investidores analisavam os resultados financeiros de mais bancos de grande porte.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: Os principais índices de Wall Street registravam ligeira queda nesta quarta-feira, depois que um relatório de inflação dos EUA com dados acima do esperado reforçou apostas em um aumento da taxa de juros neste mês, enquanto investidores analisavam os resultados financeiros de mais bancos de grande porte. Os dados mostraram que os preços ao consumidor nos EUA aceleraram em setembro em meio a um aumento nos custos da gasolina, levando operadores a reforçarem as apostas em um aumento das taxas em outubro. Eles agora veem uma chance de 46% de um aumento de 0,25 ponto percentual, em comparação com uma chance de 21,6% antes da divulgação dos números, de acordo com dados compilados pela LSEG. “Isso certamente aumenta as chances de o Federal Reserve elevar os juros na reunião de outubro, mas acredito que eles não o farão, pois nunca tivemos dois aumentos de juros em um intervalo de dois meses antes das eleições de meio de mandato”, disse Sam Stovall, estrategista-chefe de investimentos da CFRA Research. Stovall disse que, como o Fed adotou uma postura mais restritiva em relação à política monetária, os dados tornam um aumento das taxas em dezembro cada vez mais provável. Os mercados também assimilavam mais uma rodada de resultados financeiros dos bancos. O Bank of America (BAC.N) registrava queda de 8,5% após o lucro da instituição financeira ter recuado no terceiro trimestre, uma vez que ela reservou US$1,2 bilhão para cobrir multas regulatórias, enquanto o Morgan Stanley (MS.N) caía 3,4%, apesar do aumento no lucro trimestral. O índice S&P 500 Banks (.SPXBK) caía 2,4%, atingindo seu nível mais baixo em mais de quatro meses. A gestora de ativos BlackRock (BLK.N) tinha alta de 2% após divulgar um salto no lucro do terceiro trimestre, impulsionado pelo aumento das comissões provenientes da gestão de fundos de clientes. Às 11h09 (horário de Brasília), o Índice Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) caía 32,80 pontos, ou 0,06%, para 51.637,30, o S&P 500 (.SPX) tinha queda de 46,65 pontos, ou 0,60%, para 7.758,80, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) recuava 216,07 pontos, ou 0,78%, para 26.988,31. Sete dos 11 principais setores do S&P 500 registravam queda. Os setores tradicionalmente considerados defensivos apresentavam alta, com as ações de bens de consumo básico (.SPLRCS) e do setor de saúde (.SPXHC) subindo 0,9% e 1,7%, respectivamente. O índice de tecnologia do S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) era negociado nos menores níveis em mais de duas semanas, à medida que as ações de fabricantes de chips voltaram a ficar sob pressão. Elas perderam terreno na terça-feira após relatos indicando avanços no projeto de chips pela empresa chinesa CXMT (688825.SS) , o que alimentou preocupações com a concorrência. As ações da Intel (INTC.O) e da Micron (MU.O) caíam 2,6% e 1%, respectivamente, enquanto a Nvidia (NVDA.O) recuava 1,7%. A maioria das ações das “Sete Magníficas” tinha queda, com exceção da Alphabet (GOOGL.O) e da Apple (AAPL.O) , que subiam 0,2% e 0,9%, respectivamente. Também estão previstas para o final do dia falas do presidente do Fed de Richmond, Tom Barkin, e a divulgação do “Livro Bege" do Fed, relatório sobre as condições econômicas regionais.

item.title: China’s funding of global development institutions rises tenfold since 2010 to $3 billion
item.description: This makes China the fifth-largest donor to the International Development Association, the World Bank’s fund for the poorest countries.
item.dc:creator: Aakriti Handa
item.content:encoded:
-->

Subscribe

Features

China’s funding of global development institutions rises tenfold since 2010 to $3 billion

This makes China the fifth-largest donor to the International Development Association, which is the World Bank’s fund for the poorest countries.

Aakriti Handa

14 October, 2026 07:07 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: China’s funding to development-focussed multilateral institutions increased to more than $3 billion in 2024, registering a ten-fold increase from $260 million in 2010, according to a study conducted by the Center for Global Development.

This makes China the fifth-largest donor to the International Development Association (IDA), which is the World Bank’s fund for the poorest countries, up from the 28th position it held in 2010.

China rose the ranks thanks to its latest pledge of a whopping $1.5 million to the latest replenishment. China’s funding to multilateral development banks or MDBs — that provide grants and loans on favourable terms to poorer countries — has increased by 92% over the past five years. MDBs are funded by multiple countries to finance large development projects that emerging economies may struggle to fund alone.

Show Full Article

The study, authored by Beata Cichocka and Ian Mitchell, also found a sharp increase in China’s multilateral climate-finance footprint, from $600 million in 2017 to $5.25 billion in 2025.

Although China’s contributions to the development-oriented multilaterals have grown more than tenfold since 2010, they remain highly selective. In other words, China is not uniformly amping up funding across various multilateral banks.

China’s contributions to development-oriented multilaterals, 2011–2024 | Screenshot: Center for Global Development study titled ‘China in the Multilateral Development System’ It ranks only 19th for voluntary contributions to the United Nations and contributes to just seven of the 26 vertical funds (like Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance; the Global Fund; or the Green Climate Fund). Its funding is concentrated in MDB concessional windows that provide loans on more generous terms, especially the International Development Association, and in climate finance. Hence, China remains a modest vertical fund donor and a limited voluntary UN funder.

Its overall contributions to vertical funds have fallen by 32 per cent.

More funding; less borrowing At the same time, China is borrowing less from development banks—its borrowing from MDBs has fallen nearly by half, from over $8 billion in 2021 to $4.7 billion in 2024. At the World Bank too, China has plummeted from being the largest borrower in 2017 to only the 18th largest borrower in 2025. In fact, the World Bank estimates that China will stop borrowing altogether after 2031.

China’s borrowing from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), a multilateral development bank it helped establish and is its largest shareholder, has also declined markedly since 2017.

However, China’s growing financial contribution has not led to it becoming more influential at these development banks. China’s voting power has largely remained unchanged since 2021.

Despite holding 6 per cent of the shares in the World Bank, it holds lesser voting power than the around 12 per cent implied by the Bank’s own shareholding formula.

In addition, Chinese nationals now hold fewer top UN jobs than they did five years ago, having lost leadership positions at WHO, ITU, UNIDO and WMO. Chinese nationals lead just two of the 56 development-relevant UN bodies examined and make up only 1.3 percent of the wider UN staff, despite China accounting for around 17 percent of the world’s population.

China is indeed neither withdrawing from the existing multilateral system nor simply replacing traditional Western donors within it. It is becoming more deeply embedded across a range of institutions—notably, the World Bank’s IDA and WHO—while engaging on terms that preserve its flexibility.

item.title: US retirees to receive 3.6% Social Security increase in 2027
item.description: Some 76 million Americans receiving Social Security and Supplemental Security Income benefits will see their monthly payments rise 3.6% in 2027, accelerating from the prior year's increase for a second straight year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Some 76 million Americans receiving Social Security and Supplemental Security Income benefits will see their monthly payments rise 3.6% in 2027, accelerating from the prior year's increase for a second straight year. The Social Security Administration announced the annual cost-of-living adjustment to benefits on Wednesday after the Bureau of Labor Statistics published the [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"Consumer Price Index"] for September. The agency bases the annual increase, closely watched by retirees and others receiving benefits, on the average of the annual increase in the CPI for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, also known as the CPI-W index. That index rose 3.9% in September and averaged about 3.6% for the three months of July, August and September. The increase takes effect in January for 72 million Social Security recipients and on December 31, 2026, for nearly 7.3 million SSI beneficiaries. Some recipients receive both Social Security and SSI benefits. For 2026, the increase was 2.8%. Inflation accelerated again this year after the US and Israel attacked Iran, causing global energy market disruptions that have sent crude [USN:L1N46003I TEXT:"oil prices"] above $100 a barrel. More recently, refined petroleum products like diesel fuel have climbed to record highs and have contributed to a widening of inflationary pressures. The more widely watched main CPI index rose 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in August, BLS said.

item.title: USA-Les prix à la consommation progressent en septembre, tirés par le carburant
item.description: L'inflation aux États-Unis a accéléré en septembre, en raison notamment de la hausse des prix des carburants, montrent les données officielles publiées mercredi.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'inflation aux États-Unis a accéléré en septembre, en raison notamment de la hausse des prix des carburants, montrent les données officielles publiées mercredi. Les prix à la consommation ont augmenté de 3,7% sur un an, alors que les économistes interrogés par Reuters tablaient sur +3,6% après une hausse de 3,4% en août. Sur un mois, les prix avancent de 0,6%, comme prévu, après +0,4% en août. La mesure dite "core" est pour sa part ressortie à +2,6% sur un an en septembre, alors que les économistes tablaient sur +2,5% après +2,4% en août. Ce rapport fait suite à des enquêtes menées ce mois-ci qui ont mis en évidence une nouvelle détérioration du moral des consommateurs et une chute de la cote de popularité de Donald Trump, alimentées par l’inquiétude face à la hausse du coût de la vie. Un sondage Reuters/Ipsos a révélé qu’environ 78% des Américains imputaient la hausse des prix, qui dépasse la progression des salaires, aux politiques de Donald Trump, notamment aux droits de douane sur les importations et au conflit entre les États-Unis et Israël d'une part et l’Iran d'autre part. Le rapport sur l’inflation de l'indice des prix à la consommation (IPC) de septembre était très attendu par des millions de retraités et d’autres bénéficiaires de la Sécurité sociale qui cherchaient à déterminer de combien leurs prestations augmenteraient l’année prochaine. L’Administration de la Sécurité sociale utilise les données de l’IPC pour les salariés urbains et les employés de bureau, couvrant la période allant du troisième trimestre 2025 au troisième trimestre 2026, afin de déterminer l’ajustement annuel au coût de la vie des prestations de Sécurité sociale et du revenu de sécurité supplémentaire (SSI) pour 2027. Ces programmes bénéficient aux retraités, ainsi qu’aux personnes en situation de handicap et à certaines veuves, certains veufs et certains enfants.

item.title: Netflix cuts about 6% of jobs in biggest layoff since 2022
item.description: Netflix is laying off 6% of its workforce, or roughly 1,000 employees, in its biggest cuts since 2022, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters, as the streaming pioneer faces tough competition for viewers from legacy rivals and YouTube.
item.dc:creator: Prathik Jayaprakash, Anzar Mehraj
item.content:encoded: Netflix (NFLX.O) is laying off 6% of its workforce, or roughly 1,000 employees, in its biggest cuts since 2022, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters, as the streaming pioneer faces tough competition for viewers from legacy rivals and YouTube. The bulk of the job cuts would be in Netflix's product, tech, legal and human-resources teams, the email Co-CEOs Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos sent to employees on Wednesday showed. "Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources," they said in the memo. "Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full-year forecast." Netflix shares, down around 25% so far this year, rose 0.7% on Wednesday. The company had about 16,000 employees at the end of last year. This year, the streaming giant has faced doubts about its ability to sustain the growth that disrupted the US media industry by putting pressure on cable TV businesses. Engagement, or the amount of time users spend on Netflix, has become a key concern for investors as platforms such as YouTube and TikTok attract viewers with free-to-watch, user-generated content that gives them a cost advantage over Netflix. A failed pursuit of Warner Bros Discovery's streaming and studio assets earlier this year deepened doubts about Netflix's strategy. Paramount completed its [USN:L4N45S0XK TEXT:"$110-billion Warner Bros acquisition"] earlier this month to form Skydance (SKYD.N) . "They haven't been able to find like another line of major revenue," said Ross Benes, senior analyst at eMarketer, adding the company remains reliant on a subscription business that could be approaching a ceiling. "Eventually, because they've kind of nearing a ceiling with that, they'll need another revenue stream to diversify, and that's where it's been more of a struggle." Netflix has been trying to expand beyond its subscription business by investing in an ad tier, live programming and gaming. Its last major round of layoffs came in 2022, when it cut about 450 jobs in two rounds after losing subscribers for the first time in more than a decade. The Wall Street Journal first reported on Wednesday's memo.

item.title: Merz: EU wird sich künftig gegen Handelsverzerrung wehren
item.description: Kurz vor dem EU-Gipfel hat Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz eine härtere EU-Handelspolitik angekündigt. Es werde "eine robuste europäische Antwort auf die wachsende Unfairness im Welthandel, auf wettbewerbsverzerrende Handelspraktiken anderer Staaten geben", sagte der CDU-Vorsitzende am Mittwoch in einer Regierungserklärung im Bundestag. Deshalb habe er gemeinsam mit dem französischen Staatspräsidenten Emmanuel Macron eine Reihe von Vorschlägen vorgelegt. "Wir sehen nicht länger tatenlos zu, wenn andere Staaten durch hohe Subventionen, künstlich abgewertete Währungen, Überkapazitäten und aggressive Preissetzung unserer Wirtschaft schaden", betonte Merz.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kurz vor dem EU-Gipfel hat Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz eine härtere EU-Handelspolitik angekündigt. Es werde "eine robuste europäische Antwort auf die wachsende Unfairness im Welthandel, auf wettbewerbsverzerrende Handelspraktiken anderer Staaten geben", sagte der CDU-Vorsitzende am Mittwoch in einer Regierungserklärung im Bundestag. Deshalb habe er gemeinsam mit dem französischen Staatspräsidenten Emmanuel Macron eine Reihe von Vorschlägen vorgelegt. "Wir sehen nicht länger tatenlos zu, wenn andere Staaten durch hohe Subventionen, künstlich abgewertete Währungen, Überkapazitäten und aggressive Preissetzung unserer Wirtschaft schaden", betonte Merz. "Wer mit uns den Handelskonflikt sucht, der wird erfahren, dass wir uns jetzt zur Wehr setzen, und zwar mit angemessenen Reaktionen", fügte er hinzu. Man plane unter anderem ein neues Handelsschutzinstrument, mit dem die EU-Kommission bei gezielten Angriffen auf Industrien und Lieferketten schnell reagieren könne. Darüber werde man auf dem EU-Gipfel diskutieren. Wie in dem deutsch-französischen Vorschlag nannte Merz in seiner Regierungserklärung keine Länder. Die Abwehrinstrumente beträfen den Umgang mit mehreren Ländern, hatte die Bundesregierung gesagt. Dazu gehören vor allem China und die USA. So sind die chinesischen Exporte im September wegen der weltweit starken Nachfrage nach Halbleitern und Autos unerwartet kräftig gestiegen. Sie wuchsen um 36,3 Prozent im Vergleich zum Vorjahresmonat, wie die Zollbehörde am Mittwoch in Peking mitteilte. Der Handelsüberschuss - Exporte minus Importe - weitete sich allein im September auf 133,53 Milliarden Dollar aus. Deshalb sind vor allem die EU-Länder in Alarmstimmung. Die Bundesregierung sieht eine EU-China-Vereinbarung zur Beschränkung des Imports chinesischer Hybrid-Autos deshalb zwar als einen Schritt in die richtige Richtung, der aber nicht ausreichend sei. "Das löst natürlich noch nicht das Problem des riesigen Handelsdefizits, das wir mit der Volksrepublik China haben", sagte ein Regierungsvertreter. Nach Informationen von Reuters arbeitet die EU-Kommission an Einfuhrbeschränkungen für Waren aus China in den Bereichen Chemie, Maschinenbau und Pharma. Merz erneuerte mit Blick auf die Debatte auf dem EU-Gipfel zum nächsten EU-Finanzrahmen seine Ablehnung der bisherigen Vorschläge der EU-Kommission und auch der irischen EU-Ratspräsidentschaft. "Es ist mein fester Wille, dass wir die Verhandlungen noch in diesem Jahr zu einem guten Abschluss bringen", sagte er einerseits. Aber die Mittel seien begrenzt. Die EU-Kommission hatte für die Jahre 2028 bis 2034 einen Finanzrahmen von rund zwei Billionen Euro vorgeschlagen. Deutschland und andere Nettozahler fordern Kürzungen um mehrere hundert Milliarden Euro. Der Finanzrahmen muss von den EU-27 einstimmig beschlossen werden. Eine Einigung wird frühestens auf einem Sondergipfel im November erwartet. Die Nettozahler kommen am Donnerstagmorgen zu einem Treffen in Brüssel zusammen. Auf dem zweitägigen EU-Gipfel soll auch über die EU-Erweiterung, weitere Hilfen für die Ukraine sowie über Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und Entbürokratisierung gesprochen werden.

item.title: Insider: Deutschland verhandelt über 50-Prozent-Anteil an KNDS
item.description: Deutschland will einem Insider zufolge angesichts schwindender Chancen auf einen baldigen Börsengang die gesamte Beteiligung der deutschen KNDS-Eigentümerfamilien an dem Panzerbauer kaufen. Die Verhandlungen mit den in der Wegmann-Holding zusammengeschlossenen Familien liefen noch, beim Preis sei man aber nicht mehr weit voneinander entfernt, sagte eine mit den Vorgängen vertraute Person der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. Das "Handelsblatt" hatte am Mittwoch berichtet, eine Entscheidung sei in den nächsten Wochen zu erwarten. Angesichts fehlender Alternativen halte die Bundesregierung die Übernahme des gesamten Anteils für sinnvoll, um eine französische Dominanz beim Hersteller des Kampfpanzers "Leopard 2" zu verhindern. Zwei Insider sagten, die Pläne für den Börsengang lägen derzeit vollständig auf Eis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Deutschland will einem Insider zufolge angesichts schwindender Chancen auf einen baldigen Börsengang die gesamte Beteiligung der deutschen KNDS-Eigentümerfamilien an dem Panzerbauer kaufen. Die Verhandlungen mit den in der Wegmann-Holding zusammengeschlossenen Familien liefen noch, beim Preis sei man aber nicht mehr weit voneinander entfernt, sagte eine mit den Vorgängen vertraute Person der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. Das "Handelsblatt" hatte am Mittwoch berichtet, eine Entscheidung sei in den nächsten Wochen zu erwarten. Angesichts fehlender Alternativen halte die Bundesregierung die Übernahme des gesamten Anteils für sinnvoll, um eine französische Dominanz beim Hersteller des Kampfpanzers "Leopard 2" zu verhindern. Zwei Insider sagten, die Pläne für den Börsengang lägen derzeit vollständig auf Eis. Die in der Wegmann-Holding zusammengeschlossenen Familien wollten bei dem Börsengang - ebenso wie der französische Staat - zehn Prozent ihrer Anteile abgeben. Zugleich sollte der deutsche Staat die übrigen 40 Prozent übernehmen, um auf Augenhöhe mit Frankreich zu sein - zu einem Preis, der sich am Emissionspreis beim Börsengang orientiert. Die milliardenschwere Emission war aber vor der Sommerpause verschoben worden, weil die Investoren nicht bereit waren, die Preisvorstellungen der Familien zu erfüllen. Sie hatten sich eine Bewertung für KNDS von rund 15 Milliarden Euro erhofft. Doch Zweifel an der Nachhaltigkeit der Aufrüstung in Europa hatten die Bewertungen von Konkurrenten wie Rheinmetall (RHMG.DE) oder CSG (CSG.AS) gedrückt. Auch im Herbst, auf den KNDS gehofft hatte, ist eine höhere Bewertung nicht zu erwarten. Die Eigentümerfamilien wollten sich dazu nicht äußern. Das Bundeswirtschaftsministerium erklärte, die Bundesregierung prüfe "zum Schutz der verteidigungsindustriellen Schlüsseltechnologie im gepanzerten Fahrzeugbau (...) den Erwerb von Anteilen auf Augenhöhe mit Frankreich". Dazu sei sie im Austausch mit allen Beteiligten. Die Bundeswehr ist der größte Auftraggeber von KNDS. Die Entscheidung über einen Verkaufsprozess liege aber bei den gegenwärtigen Aktionären, betonte das Ministerium. KNDS selbst teilte mit, ein Börsengang bleibe das Ziel des deutsch-französischen Konzerns. Zu möglichen Gesprächen zwischen der Bundesregierung und den Familien nehme KNDS keine Stellung.

item.title: Sportradar hit by EU, UK antitrust complaints from rival
item.description: BRUSSELS, Oct 14 : Sports technology company Sportradar Group was hit with antitrust complaints to EU and UK regulators on Wednesday by sportsbook software company Altenar Technologies, which accused it of blocking rivals' access to its live official sports data. Swiss-headquartered Sportradar is a leading

BRUSSELS, Oct 14 : Sports technology company Sportradar Group was hit with antitrust complaints to EU and UK regulators on Wednesday by sportsbook software company Altenar Technologies, which accused it of blocking rivals' access to its live official sports data. Swiss-headquartered Sportradar is a leading content provider of betting-related content in major sports including tennis, soccer and basketball. Its exclusive deals with major sports leagues MLB, NBA, ATP, and NHL include data collection and distribution rights, as well as the right to provide live betting odds derived from that data. The complaints follow an antitrust lawsuit Altenar filed in a US court in April, alleging Sportradar has monopolised the market for live official sports data in the US and stifled competition.

Sportradar declined to comment. Britain's Competition and Markets Authority said it does not comment on specific examples or scenarios outside of a formal investigation. The European Commission did not immediately respond to a request for comment. "We believe Sportradar is using its control of essential sports data to shut out businesses with a competing offer," an Altenar spokesperson said. "Bookmakers across the EU and UK need a choice of suppliers and a market that supports competition and innovation. We are asking the European Commission and the CMA to intervene and ensure that independent providers can compete on fair terms," the spokesperson said. Altenar is also asking the CMA to impose interim measures restoring access to essential data and odds pending the outcome of an investigation. EU antitrust violations can result in fines of up to 10 per cent of a company's annual global turnover.

item.title: Airbus jetmaking CEO sees early decision on higher A350 output
item.description: Airbus plans to decide "sooner rather than later" on increased production capacity for its A350 wide-body jet, its commercial CEO Lars Wagner said, part of a trio of relatively near-term decisions for the planemaker as its rivalry with Boeing intensifies.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Airbus (AIR.PA) plans to decide "sooner rather than later" on increased production capacity for its A350 wide-body jet, its commercial CEO Lars Wagner said, part of a trio of relatively near-term decisions for the planemaker as its rivalry with Boeing intensifies. The world's largest planemaker is also actively studying launching bigger versions of the A350 as well as its smallest model, the loss-making A220, with decisions on both projects expected towards the beginning of a five-year planning period. "The decision for an increased rate on the A350 is inevitable. We're going to do it because the market clearly demands more aircraft," Wagner told a news briefing. "It's a big decision, so we need to bring it to the board of directors. But this is going to happen rather sooner than later." Airbus has one assembly line for the carbon-fibre jet, designed to compete with Boeing's lightweight 787 and delayed 777X. The plant was designed to handle 12 to 13 jets a month. Going higher would need a new line and industrial system, Wagner said. Separately, he said, there is "clearly demand" for a longer A350 with more seats, widely dubbed the A350-2000, and a bigger version of the roughly 130-seat A220, known as the A220-500. The former MTU Aero Engines CEO, who took the helm of Airbus' largest division this year, declined to say whether Airbus might loosen Rolls-Royce's (RR.L) position as sole engine maker on the A350 when it comes to powering the new version. Industry sources say Airbus has toyed with using an engine from GE Aerospace for the roughly 400-seat A350-2000, but that the engine maker has so far shown limited interest in joining. Wagner reiterated that Airbus was confident of reaching its year-end delivery goals despite recent industrial quality flaws. Longer term, Airbus continues to look at a "notional" date of 2030 for launching an all-new single-aisle jet, he said.

item.title: 米9月ＣＰＩ、前年比＋3.7％に加速 利上げ観測再浮上
item.description:
Lucia Mutikani
[ワシントン １４日 ロイター] - 米労働省労働統計局が１４日発表した９月の米消費者物...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米9月ＣＰＩ、前年比＋3.7％に加速　利上げ観測再浮上 10/14 21:59 配信

ニューヨーク市内の食料品店、8月26日撮影 REUTERS/Jeenah Moon/File Photo/File Photo

Lucia Mutikani

[ワシントン　１４日　ロイター] - 米労働省労働統計局が１４日発表した９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前月比０．６％、前年比では３．７％上昇し、前月の０．４％と３．４％上昇から加速した。ガソリン価格の急騰を背景に伸びが加速した。１１月の中間選挙を控えたトランプ大統領と共和党に打撃となるほか、１０月中の利上げの可能性が再び意識される状況となった。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は、前月比０．６％上昇、前年同月比３．６％上昇だった。

ＬＰＬフィナンシャルのチーフエコノミスト、ジェフリー・ローチ氏は「目標回帰に向けた『ラストマイル』は依然として険しく、金利は高止まりする可能性がある」と指摘。「物価安定への道筋は一段と見通しにくくなっており、今回の内容は連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が今月開く連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での判断を複雑にする」と述べた。

９月はガソリン価格が９．１％急騰し、前月比でのＣＰＩ上昇の半分以上を占めた。食品価格は変わらず。７月と８月はいずれも０．１％上昇していた。食料品店の価格は前月比０．１％下落したものの、前年比では１．８％上昇した。牛肉価格が１．０％、乳製品および関連製品の価格が０．９％それぞれ下落した。一方、アルコール以外の飲料は０．９％、果物・野菜は０．５％それぞれ値上がりした。

＜コアインフレ予想上回る＞

変動の大きい食品とエネルギーを除くコアＣＰＩは前月比０．３％上昇し８月と変わらず。伸びはロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想（０．２％上昇）を上回った。前年比では２．６％上昇し、前月の２．４％から加速した。

コアＣＰＩは、家賃や宿泊費などを含む住居費が０．４％上昇したことが押し上げ要因となった。持ち家の帰属家賃は０．３％上昇した。

中古車・トラックの価格は０．７％上昇。ジェット燃料価格の上昇を受けて航空運賃も１．２％上昇した。衣料品価格も０．３％上昇した。

ＦＲＢはインフレ指標として、個人消費支出（ＰＣＥ）価格指数を重視している。構成品目の比重が異なるため、コアＣＰＩの上昇率は、８月に３．０％上昇したコアＰＣＥ価格指数を下回っている。

ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、金融市場が織り込む１０月２７─２８日のＦＯＭＣでの利上げ確率は約５２％と、ＣＰＩ発表前の約２２％から上昇した。９月の雇用者数の伸び鈍化や、７月と８月のＰＣＥ価格指数が予想を下回ったことを受け、今月の利上げ確率は一時低下していた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：食品値下げは広がるのか、日銀判断にも影響する分岐点に コラム：ＦＲＢが物価2.0％目指せば、利下げ開始は大幅遅延に コラム：市場の米利下げ織り込み、昨年と同様に過剰ならドル150円も＝佐々木融氏 コラム：マイナス金利解除後の政策占うＣＰＩ、上下2つのシナリオ コラム：下げ止まらない日本円の購買力、失地回復への処方箋は＝植野大作氏 最終更新: 10/14(水) 23:40 ロイター

item.title: Container ship sinks near Hormuz after being hit by projectile
item.description: A Singapore-flagged container ship has sunk near the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by a projectile, while a dry bulk carrier damaged in an earlier attack is also reported to be sinking, maritime security sources said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Saul, Renee Maltezou
item.content:encoded: A Singapore-flagged container ship has sunk near the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by a projectile, while a dry bulk carrier damaged in an earlier attack is also reported to be sinking, maritime security sources said on Wednesday. Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days. The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride, a small container vessel with capacity for 2,824 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU), sank while sailing through the strait, the sources said. "GFS PRIDE sustained damage and a fire on board, and has since sunk. All 21 crew members were safely evacuated. No injuries have been reported," the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) said in a statement on Wednesday, adding that the vessel had been sailing through the strait on Tuesday. The loss of the GFS Pride marks the second vessel to sink since the US-Iran war began on February 28, according to data from the UN shipping agency, the International Maritime Organization. "MPA is deeply concerned about the continued attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz," the Singapore authority said. "Such attacks are unprovoked, unjustifiable, and a breach of international law." GFS Pride's United Arab Emirates-based manager, GFS Ship Management FZE, could not be immediately reached for comment. The latest incident comes amid a sharp escalation in threats to commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade passed before the war. Tehran has sought to tighten its grip on the waterway since U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, restricting transit in an effort to gain leverage over Washington. The United States, meanwhile, has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and expanded sanctions to intensify economic pressure on Tehran. Iran is increasingly deploying new tactics against vessels transiting the strait as it seeks to keep oil prices elevated and influence US midterm elections, [USN:L8N45Z15J TEXT:"two senior Iranian officials told Reuters."] While Iran and the US have focused their attacks on tankers, cargo and container vessels have also been attacked, immobilised or sunk. In a separate incident, the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged Cape Dao was reported to be sinking close to the strait after being struck by a projectile on September 23, the maritime security sources said. "The Antigua & Barbuda flagged bulk carrier CAPE DAO, originally hit on the 23 September, is reported to be sinking after an unsuccessful rescue attempt," British maritime risk management group Vanguard said in a note on Wednesday. The vessel's UAE-based manager Peonies Shipmanagement FZE could not be immediately reached for comment. The Maltese-flagged container ship Safeen Prestige was hit by a projectile in March and later sank north of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guards attacked and seized the container ship MSC Francesca in April.

item.title: 日本が最大210億ドル投資へ、ＮＹ州に半導体2工場 ＧＦ運営
item.description:
Stephen Nellis Makiko Yamazaki David Shepardson

item.content:encoded:
日本が最大210億ドル投資へ、ＮＹ州に半導体2工場　ＧＦ運営 10/14 21:46 配信

半導体チップのイメージ写真、2023年撮影 REUTERS/Florence Lo/Illustration//File Photo

Stephen Nellis　Makiko Yamazaki　David Shepardson

[ニューヨーク １４日 ロイター] - 日本は米ニューヨーク（ＮＹ）州に半導体工場を２カ所建設するために最大２１０億ドルを投資する。これらの工場は日米で共同保有し、半導体受託生産大手のグローバルファウンドリーズ（ＧＦ）が運営する。同社が１４日に発表した。

米国が日本車などの輸入品に対する関税を少なくとも２５％から１５％に引き下げる見返りとして、日本が５５００億ドルを対米投資することで合意した枠組みの一環。

ＧＦによると、米政府は新たな半導体工場の持ち分を取得するが、投資資金は全て日本が提供する。

アブダビの政府系ファンドであるムバダラ・インベストメントが過半株式を保有する同社は、工場の建設と運営、工場への半導体製造技術のライセンス供与から手数料を得る。

別の合意に基づき、米政府はＧＦの株式４％を取得し、同社に対する米国の保有比率は約７％になる。ＧＦのティム・ブリーン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）がロイターに明らかにした。

ブリーン氏によると、ＧＦが顧客関係を管理し、ＮＹ工場の初期顧客には日本のルネサスエレクトロニクスと米アップルが含まれる。

同氏は「米国と日本の顧客を優先したいと考えている」と説明。「最終的には米日以外の企業からも需要が見込まれると思うが、どの企業にどの期間で何を提供するのかを最終決定するプロセスを経ていくことになる」と述べた。

日本はこれまで、この投資制度の下で総額１０００億ドルを超える２つのプロジェクト群を発表している。

米国との取り決めに基づき、トランプ米大統領は日本が資金提供するプロジェクトを選定する。投資から得られる利用可能なフリーキャッシュフローは、日米双方が一定額を回収するまでは両国間で均等に分配され、その後は９０％が米国に配分される。

ブリーン氏は、日本からの資本投資の少なくとも一部は、東京エレクトロンなどの半導体製造装置メーカーや、米企業と並んでサプライチェーン（供給網）を支配する他の日本企業に利益還元されると述べた。

「もちろん、日本の機器サプライヤーがこの取り組みに参加することには強い関心を持っている」とし、「われわれは非常に柔軟な姿勢で臨むが、日本のエコシステムとは積極的に関わっていくだろう。なぜなら、彼らは素晴らしい技術を持っているからだ」と述べた。

item.title: Fed rate hike call seen tight as inflation heats up
item.description: A Federal Reserve interest-rate decision later this month may be a closer call than previously thought after Labor Department data showed consumer prices were up 3.7% last month from a year earlier, well above the Fed's 2% target and moving in the wrong direction.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: A Federal Reserve interest-rate decision later this month may be a closer call than previously thought after Labor Department data showed consumer prices were up 3.7% last month from a year earlier, well above the Fed's 2% target and moving in the wrong direction. Higher gasoline prices from the Middle East war were a main driver. Excluding volatile food and energy prices, the core Consumer Price Index (CPI) was up 2.6%, more than the 2.5% economists polled by Reuters had projected. The Fed lifted the policy rate in September to a target range of 3.75%-4.00% to bring down too-high inflation, and officials have said they are looking closely for signs of broadening price pressures that could keep inflation high even if gas prices fall, necessitating more policy tightening. Wednesday's data contained plenty of such signs. "The surprise was not concentrated in any one item, like it was with wireless in the August report, but instead reflected a number of components showing strength, i.e., it was broad-based," wrote Omair Sharif, founder of Inflation Insights. Software prices were up 28% from a year earlier, the largest increase ever, and toy prices also notched a record rise, the data showed -- emblematic of inflationary impulses from both AI-driven demand and higher tariffs under the Trump administration. "This means that inflation is broadening out, something that is not a good omen for the Fed and would raise the probability for an increase in rates at the end of the October FOMC meeting," wrote Raymond James Chief Economist Eugenio Aleman, referring to the Fed's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee, which next meets October 27-28. In recent weeks several of the Fed's most influential policymakers have signaled there's time to weigh more data before delivering what most believe will be at least one more rate hike by year's end, and traders had bet heavily against a second straight hike under Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh -- especially just a week before November elections that will decide if Trump's Republican party holds on to majorities in Congress. After Wednesday's economic data, interest-rate futures are priced for around even odds of an October rate hike, a place of unusual uncertainty around the outcome of a Fed decision just two weeks away. Fed policymakers are also weighing the risk of tightening too fast and unduly slowing the labor market. Unemployment has been low, but job gains have also cooled. "September CPI keeps inflation concerns alive, with core inflation still sticky, but weaker jobs data and fragile consumer sentiment mean the Fed still has room to hold in October," PPHC Chief Economist Martin Beck said.

NEW YORK, Oct 14 : Japan will invest up to $21 billion in two chip factories in New York state that will be jointly owned by the US government and Japanese interests and operated by GlobalFoundries, the company said on Wednesday.   Shares of the Malta, New York-based company rose more than 4 per cent in early trading. They have gained more than 33 per cent this year. The move is part of a deal for Japan to invest $550 billion in the US struck by President Donald Trump's administration last year in return for the US lowering tariffs on Japanese cars and other imports from at least 25 per cent to 15 per cent.  The US will take a stake in the new chip factories, but Japan will provide all of the investment capital, GlobalFoundries said.

The company, which is majority-owned by Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund Mubadala Investment Co, will earn fees from building and operating the factories, as well as licensing chip manufacturing technology to them.  In a separate agreement, the US government will take a 4 per cent stake in GlobalFoundries, bringing its total ownership of the chipmaker to about 7 per cent, GlobalFoundries CEO Tim Breen told Reuters. Breen said GlobalFoundries would manage customer relationships, and initial customers for the New York factories include Japan's Renesas Electronics and iPhone maker Apple.   "We definitely would like to give priority to US and Japanese customers," he said. "Ultimately, I expect other companies that aren't US and Japanese will also be part of the demand, but we'll obviously go through a process after announcement to finalize the exact who gets what over what timeframe." Japan has so far announced two batches of projects worth over $100 billion combined under the investment scheme. Under the arrangement with the US, Trump selects projects to be funded by Japan. Available free cash flows from investments will be split evenly between the two countries until a specific allocation is reached, after which 90 per cent will go to the US. GlobalFoundries' Breen said that at least some of the capital investment by Japan will flow back to chip-manufacturing toolmakers such as Tokyo Electron and other Japanese firms that along with US rivals dominate the supply chain. "Obviously, we have a strong interest in the Japanese equipment suppliers to be part of it," Breen said. "We will be very open-minded, but we'll definitely engage very much with the Japanese ecosystem because they have great technologies."

Source: Reuters

Oct 14 : Hyundai Motor India plans to invest 110 billion rupees ($1.16 billion) in its Pune city plant to scale up the facility's annual production capacity by nearly 90 per cent by 2030, the automaker said on Wednesday.  The move comes a day after parent Hyundai Motor Group said it would invest $15.5 billion in India through 2032, positioning the world's third-largest car market as a key growth market.  India is drawing billions of dollars in commitments from global automakers eager to capture rising consumer demand and strengthen their manufacturing footprints. item.title: Morgan Stanley übertrifft Gewinnerwartungen dank Aktienhandel
item.description: Die US-Investmentbank Morgan Stanley hat im dritten Quartal dank eines starken Aktienhandels mehr verdient als erwartet. Das auf die Aktionäre entfallende Ergebnis stieg um 6,5 Prozent auf 4,91 Milliarden Dollar oder 3,03 Dollar je Aktie, wie das Institut am Mittwoch mitteilte. Analysten hatten laut Daten des Anbieters LSEG lediglich mit einem Gewinn von 2,91 Dollar je Aktie gerechnet. Die Nettoerträge kletterten um 11,6 Prozent auf 20,34 Milliarden Dollar.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die US-Investmentbank Morgan Stanley (MS.N) hat im dritten Quartal dank eines starken Aktienhandels mehr verdient als erwartet. Das auf die Aktionäre entfallende Ergebnis stieg um 6,5 Prozent auf 4,91 Milliarden Dollar oder 3,03 Dollar je Aktie, wie das Institut am Mittwoch mitteilte. Analysten hatten laut Daten des Anbieters LSEG lediglich mit einem Gewinn von 2,91 Dollar je Aktie gerechnet. Die Nettoerträge kletterten um 11,6 Prozent auf 20,34 Milliarden Dollar. Morgan Stanley profitierte von der hohen Volatilität an den Finanzmärkten. Auslöser der Kursschwankungen waren die Zinsentscheidung der US-Notenbank Fed sowie der Krieg zwischen den USA und dem Iran, die Anleger zu Umschichtungen ihrer Portfolios veranlassten. Bereits am [USN:L8N45Z1C1 TEXT:"Dienstag"] hatten einige andere Banken ein ähnliches Bild gezeichnet. Während Goldman Sachs (GS.N) und die Citigroup (C.N) ihre Gewinne unerwartet deutlich steigerten, verfehlte jedoch der Branchenprimus JPMorgan (JPM.N) wegen eines schwächeren Investmentbankings die Erwartungen. Wells Fargo (WFC.N) übertraf zwar die Gewinnziele, enttäuschte Anleger jedoch bei den Erträgen und dem Zinsüberschuss. Die Bank of America (BAC.N) berichtete am [USN:L8N4601CK TEXT:"Mittwoch"] von einem Gewinneinbruch infolge eines schwachen Kapitalmarktgeschäfts und einer Milliardenstrafe. Bei Morgan Stanley war Treiber der Entwicklung der Aktienhandel, dessen Einnahmen um fast 41 Prozent auf 5,8 Milliarden Dollar in die Höhe schnellten. Im Anleihehandel verzeichnete Morgan Stanley hingegen einen Rückgang der Erträge um 7,3 Prozent auf 2,01 Milliarden Dollar. VERMÖGENSVERWALTUNG UNTER ERWARTUNGEN Im wichtigen Geschäft mit der Vermögensverwaltung stiegen die Einnahmen zwar um 10,1 Prozent auf 9,07 Milliarden Dollar, blieben damit aber leicht unter den Erwartungen. "Das ist bedeutsam, da die Vermögensverwaltung einer der wichtigsten strategischen Wachstumsmotoren der Bank ist", erklärte Marktexperte Daniel Coatsworth vom Broker AJ Bell. Morgan Stanley hatte den Bereich in den vergangenen Jahren ausgebaut, um die Abhängigkeit vom schwankungsanfälligen Investmentbanking und dem Handel zu verringern. Das Investmentbanking behauptete sich in einem schwierigen Umfeld. Obwohl das weltweite Volumen von Fusionen und Übernahmen gegenüber dem Vorquartal um 41 Prozent einbrach und der Markt für Börsengänge gedämpft blieb, legten die Erträge der Sparte um zwei Prozent auf 2,16 Milliarden Dollar zu. Morgan Stanley agierte unter anderem als führender Finanzberater beim Kauf des deutschen Lieferdienstes Delivery Hero (DHER.DE) durch Uber (UBER.N) für 14,8 Milliarden Dollar. Zudem sicherte sich das Institut bei den erwarteten Börsengängen der Firmen für Künstliche Intelligenz (KI), Anthropic und OpenAI, Plätze in den Bankenkonsortien. Dagegen sanken die Nettoerträge in der Investment-Management-Sparte, in der auch die Privatkreditfonds gebündelt sind, auf 1,46 Milliarden Dollar nach 1,65 Milliarden vor Jahresfrist. Vor dem Hintergrund von Befürchtungen, dass KI-Technologie Softwareunternehmen in den Portfolios schaden könnte, verlangten Anleger Gelder aus einem wichtigen Fonds zurück.

item.title: Le Portugal choisit Lufthansa, et non Air France-KLM, pour prendre 44,9% de TAP
item.description: Le gouvernement portugais a annoncé mercredi avoir choisi Lufthansa pour acquérir une participation de 44,9% dans la compagnie TAP Air Portugal, pour 1,2 milliard d'euros, Lisbonne préférant ainsi la compagnie allemande à Air France-KLM , qui avait également soumis une offre.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le gouvernement portugais a annoncé mercredi avoir choisi Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) pour acquérir une participation de 44,9% dans la compagnie TAP Air Portugal, pour 1,2 milliard d'euros, Lisbonne préférant ainsi la compagnie allemande à Air France-KLM (AIRF.PA) , qui avait également soumis une offre. Cet accord, qui a mis des années à se concrétiser et qui a été reporté à plusieurs reprises, constitue une nouvelle étape dans la consolidation du secteur aérien européen, un processus jugé nécessaire pour aider les petites compagnies nationales à gagner en résilience au sein de groupes plus importants. Selon les analystes et les dirigeants du secteur, cette consolidation devrait s'accélérer, la flambée des prix du kérosène, liée à la guerre en Iran, contraignant les compagnies aériennes les plus fragiles à s'associer à des groupes plus importants et mieux capitalisés. Lufthansa, qui détient déjà Austrian Airlines, ITA Airways et SWISS, et Air France-KLM avaient soumis fin septembre des offres finales revues à la hausse . Le Premier ministre portugais Luis Montenegro a déclaré lors d'une conférence de presse que l'offre retenue dépassait de 16% celle d’Air France-KLM. "Bien que le groupe (Air France-KLM) soit naturellement déçu de ne pas avoir été retenu, il se félicite du dialogue constructif qui a eu lieu tout au long du processus", a dit un porte-parole d’Air France-KLM à Reuters. S'exprimant lors du World Aviation Festival à Lisbonne avant l'annonce, le directeur général de TAP, Luis Rodrigues, a déclaré que rejoindre un groupe plus important permettrait à la compagnie portugaise "d'accéder à un plus grand nombre de ressources à un meilleur rapport qualité-prix". Le gouvernement portugais a précisé que sa décision reposait non seulement sur le prix, mais aussi sur le plan industriel de chaque soumissionnaire pour TAP - y compris sa stratégie en matière de croissance et de viabilité à long terme de la compagnie aérienne. Le principal atout de TAP réside dans ses liaisons reliant Lisbonne au Brésil, à l'Afrique lusophone et aux États-Unis. En juin, TAP exploitait une flotte de 101 appareils desservant 93 destinations à travers le monde. La compagnie aérienne a transporté un nombre record de 8,2 millions de passagers au premier semestre 2026, en hausse de 4,2% par rapport à l'année précédente.

AIサイバーセキュリティの文字とキーボード・ロボットの腕 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration//File Photo

Padraic Halpin　Foo Yun Chee

［ダブリン　１４日　ロイター］ - 米グーグルの人工知能（ＡＩ）開発部門グーグルディープマインドの創業者で会長のデミス・ハサビス氏は１４日、ＡＩエージェントによる最近のハッキング事案は「早期の警告」だとし、システムの安全性を高めなければ、世界は近く重大な事案に直面する恐れがあると警告した。

オープンＡＩやアンソロピックのＡＩエージェントの「暴走」が相次ぎ明らかになっている。

ハサビス氏はダブリンで開かれたＡＩサミットで「（ハッキング事案は）われわれにとって早期の警告だ」と述べた。システムがまだそれほど強力ではないため、事案もそれほど重大ではないが「業界として、また個々の企業や政府がシステムの安全確保にさらに取り組まなければ、来年（２０２７年）やその先の数年を見据えると、（重大な事案に）なる可能性がある」と指摘した。

生物学や原子力など他の分野では重要なシステムを守るためのベストプラクティス（最善の慣行）が取り入れられているとし、ＡＩでそれを導入するには「やるべきことが多い」と指摘。いずれ何らかの国際的な基準策定機関が必要になるとの考えを示した。

同氏はグーグルの親会社アルファベットの最高科学責任者も務めている。２０２４年には、タンパク質の設計と構造予測でノーベル化学賞を受賞した。

マイクロソフトのブラッド・スミス社長は同じ会議で、ＡＩの不正な振る舞いによって２０２６年は「厳しい現実を思い知らされた年」になったと述べた。安全性を技術革新に追いつかせるため、ＡＩの安全性に関する新たな法律や規則が早急に必要だと指摘した。

「いかなる企業や技術も法を超越すべきではない。われわれには法律が必要であり、規制が必要だ。規制は合理的でバランスが取れたものでなければならず、技術革新も考慮しなければならない」と述べた。

「業界の一部には規制アレルギーがあるが、克服する必要がある」とした。

ハサビス氏は、国際的な基準策定機関の設置は当然の対応策に見えるとした上で、技術革新を阻害しないよう、きめ細かく機動的なものにする必要があると述べた。

「つまり基本的には、われわれが認識するリスクに見合い、技術の進む方向に応じて素早く変えられるような認証の仕組みを、柔軟に築いていく必要がある」と語った。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
日中韓の中銀総裁、バンコクで会合開催　経済・金融情勢で意見交換 10/14 20:33 配信

日銀の植田和男総裁。９月１８日、東京の日銀本店で撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Kim Kyung-Hoon）

Takahiko Wada

［東京　１４日　ロイター］ - 日銀は１４日、中国、韓国と３カ国の中央銀行総裁会合を開いたと発表した。タイのバンコクで開催中の世界銀行・国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）総会に合わせ、同日会談した。

韓国銀行の申鉉松総裁が議長を務め、中国人民銀行の潘功勝総裁、日銀の植田和男総裁が出席して最近の経済・金融情勢について意見交換した。

同会合は定期的に開催されており、今回が１５回目。次回は来年、中国人民銀が主催する予定。

item.description:
Selena Li
[バンコク １４日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のボウマン副議長（金融監督担当）は...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米ＦＲＢ、追加措置を急ぐ必要ない＝ボウマン副議長 10/14 20:26 配信

ボウマンＦＲＢ副議長、6月4日撮影 REUTERS/Kylie Cooper/File Photo

Selena Li

[バンコク １４日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のボウマン副議長（金融監督担当）は１４日、追加措置を決定する前に、前回の利上げ後の金融市場や経済の動向を見極める時間的余裕があるとの見方を示した。

ボウマン氏はバンコクで開催されている国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行会合の際に「現時点で追加行動を急ぐ必要は感じていない。時間をかけて、状況がどう変化していくかを見極める必要がある」と述べた。

人工知能（ＡＩ）が銀行にもたらすサイバーセキュリティー上のリスクに関する議論とは別に、ＦＲＢはデータセンターの開発・建設に実際に投じられる銀行をはじめとする資金源からの資金にも目を向けていると指摘。「銀行システムへの監督・規制を通じて、将来の経済を支える資金が確保される必要がある」と語った。

また、自ら指示したシリコンバレー銀行の２０２３年の破綻に関する検証を踏まえ、監督を改善してＦＲＢ内の説明責任を強化するための「全面的な組織再編」を求めた。

item.title: Ukraine says SpaceX hampers drones for attack and defence, as US ties fray
item.description: Ukraine said Elon Musk's SpaceX had limited Starlink services on Wednesday, hampering Ukrainian drones for attack missions and air defences, as relations between Kyiv and Washington have taken a sharp turn for the worse.
item.dc:creator: Yuliia Dysa, Dan Peleschuk
item.content:encoded: Ukraine said Elon Musk's SpaceX had limited Starlink services on Wednesday, hampering Ukrainian drones for attack missions and air defences, as relations between Kyiv and Washington have taken a sharp turn for the worse. Russia rained more missiles and drones down on Ukrainian cities, knocking out electricity for hundreds of thousands of people in attacks President Volodymyr Zelenskiy called "ostentatious disrespect" to Donald Trump's call for an energy ceasefire. The US president publicly turned on Zelenskiy in recent days after abruptly lifting sanctions on Russian diesel last week, under political pressure to lower fuel prices that have soared since he launched a war against Iran. He has called on Kyiv to halt attacks on Russian refineries, and said Ukrainians should replace their wartime leader. Trump announced at the weekend that Ukraine and Russia both agreed to halt attacks on energy targets, although neither side confirmed this and the past two days have seen intensive Russian bombing, including of Ukrainian power stations. After a night of bombardment of the capital Kyiv, Russian strikes continued throughout the day on Wednesday with six people killed in the western city of Lutsk, where the regional governor said a warehouse and a residential building were hit. Ukraine, for its part, continued long-range strikes on Russia, hitting [USN:L8N46009S TEXT:"Russia's biggest data centre"], although it says it is holding back from hitting energy targets for now to show respect for Trump. NO WARNING BEFORE STARLINK CUTS Ukrainian military officials said Musk's SpaceX (SPCX.O) had without warning interrupted functioning of military-grade Starlink terminals when they are moving at high speed. Kyiv installs Starlink receptors in many of its drones as part of their onboard guidance systems. Starlink operates across Ukraine, including in territory held by Russian forces. "Our defence forces did not receive a warning about this limitation, and this led to the disruption of several missions," presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov wrote on Telegram. The speed cutoff hampers Ukraine's ability to conduct strikes on Russian targets inside Ukraine, and to defend itself from Russian drones using its own interceptor drones, according to a defence ministry source and another military source. Beskrestnov said SpaceX had imposed a speed limit of 160 km per hour. The defence ministry source told Reuters military units had reported guidance systems losing their connections at speeds of less than half that. SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The defence ministry source said Ukraine was in contact with the company as well as the US government and NATO to seek clarification over the sudden limitations. The suggestion that Musk's company had limited Ukrainian military capabilities drew a sharp response from Poland, which pays for Ukrainian Starlink subscriptions on Kyiv's behalf. "Hey, @elonmusk, big man, are you playing politics with your products again?" Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski asked Musk on X. "As your European customers, we are watching you." There was no immediate response from Musk, who in the past has called Sikorski a "small man". Shares in European satellite operator Eutelsat (ETL.PA) , which is seen as Europe's best shot at taking on Starlink, [USN:L6N4600QK TEXT:"jumped on Wednesday"] as some investors bet that European providers could benefit from growing strains between Washington and Kyiv. Musk is a close political ally of Trump, and the suggestion that SpaceX might limit Ukrainian capabilities reinforced wider Ukrainian concerns that Washington could withhold battlefield support to compel its one-time ally to make concessions. Sources have told Reuters and other media that the US has threatened to cut off intelligence for early warning of missile strikes on Ukraine, to press Kyiv to suspend attacks on Russian oil refineries. NO WARNING AHEAD OF MISSILES Rescue workers in Kyiv were stretchering the injured from the wreckage of a blasted-out residential building overnight, while firefighters battled a huge blaze in the darkness. Officials said 2 people were killed and 21 wounded at the site. Some 600,000 people were left without power as Russian missiles careened into power stations during hours of attacks that primarily targeted Kyiv and Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city. Russia's defence ministry confirmed it had struck four power plants in and around Kyiv and two in Kharkiv, among other targets. Zelenskiy said 30 energy facilities were damaged. Ukrainian officials said late on Tuesday they had received no warnings from Western partners for a second day before Russian missiles hit the capital. Trump had insisted on Tuesday that Washington was [USN:L1N45Z0GP TEXT:"still sharing intelligence"]. Zelenskiy cast the latest Russian attacks as a deliberate snub to Trump's declaration of a ceasefire on energy targets. "Russia does not consider the American President's statements strong," Zelenskiy wrote on X. "The strike was entirely deliberate and demonstrative in its scale – Russia has never before shown such ostentatious disrespect toward the United States." Zelenskiy has said Ukraine is willing to observe an energy ceasefire and has not targeted Russian refineries since Trump announced it, but will not continue to hold back if Russia ignores the purported truce. The Kremlin said on Tuesday that contacts were continuing about an energy truce. Ukraine reported downing just 4 out of 39 Russian missiles, reflecting Kyiv's weakened air-defences against fast-moving ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones amid a shortage of weapons.

item.title: Lufthansa wins race for €1.2 billion stake in Portuguese carrier TAP
item.description: Portugal's government on Wednesday picked Lufthansa to buy a stake of up to 49.9% in TAP Air Portugal for €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) over rival Air France-KLM , making the German airline the strategic partner of one of Europe's last unaligned flag carriers.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves, Joanna Plucinska
item.content:encoded: Portugal's government on Wednesday picked Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) to buy a stake of up to 49.9% in TAP Air Portugal for €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) over rival Air France-KLM (AIRF.PA) , making the German airline the strategic partner of one of Europe's last unaligned flag carriers. The deal, years in the making and repeatedly delayed, is the next step in the [USN:L6N42E079 TEXT:"consolidation"] of Europe's airline industry, a process seen as necessary to help smaller national carriers become more resilient as part of larger groups. Analysts and industry executives say that is likely to accelerate as soaring jet fuel prices linked to the war in Iran force weaker airlines to work with larger, better-capitalised groups. Lufthansa, which already owns Austrian Airlines, ITA Airways and SWISS among other carriers, beat rival Air France-KLM after both airlines submitted improved final bids in late September. "This will give them an additional hub, albeit in a sphere of influence where they've lacked reach currently," said aviation analyst John Strickland, as Lufthansa will gain further access to Southwest Europe and other parts of the world by extension. TAP's main attraction is its valuable landing slots connecting Lisbon with Brazil, Portuguese-speaking Africa and the US, routes that underpin Portugal's diaspora ties, tourism flows and investment links. Prime Minister Luis Montenegro told a news briefing the winning bid exceeded Air France-KLM's offer by 16%. Speaking at the World Aviation Festival in Lisbon before the announcement, TAP CEO Luis Rodrigues said joining a larger group would allow the Portuguese carrier to "access a larger pool of resources at better value". THE PERKS The government said its decision was based not only on price but also on each bidder's industrial plan for TAP, including its strategy for the airline's growth and long-term sustainability. It wants TAP's partner to expand operations and connectivity across Portugal's airport network, not only at Lisbon's hub but also in Porto, Faro, the Azores and Madeira. Infrastructure Minister Miguel Pinto Luz said the Lufthansa Group has committed to increasing TAP's fleet to 117 aircraft by 2035 and 130 after 2035, when Lisbon's new airport is expected to be operational. As of June, TAP operated a fleet of 101 aircraft serving 93 destinations worldwide — 52 in Europe, 16 in South and Central America, 14 in Africa and 11 in North America. TAP carried a record 8.2 million passengers in the first half of 2026, up 4.2% from a year earlier, while operating revenue rose 4.3%. A ROCKY ROAD AHEAD Analysts pointed to Lufthansa's ongoing financial woes as a potential challenge in TAP's turnaround. Such deals require initial investment, and the pay-off isn't always guaranteed. "Lufthansa is still struggling financially. Lufthansa Deutsche Airlines, as the largest part of the group, is still losing money. It has to get its own house in order," Strickland told Reuters. Lufthansa has vowed to reach an operating profit of 8% to 10% between 2028 and 2030 and to simplify and centralise its operations in an effort to rebuild investor confidence. The turnaround of Italy's ITA is still ongoing, too, Strickland said, with investors and analysts previously worrying about the impact of Lufthansa's fragmented and spread-out network. (This story has been corrected to clarify that the plan is to expand TAP’s fleet to 117 aircraft, not by 117 aircraft, in paragraph 11.)

item.title: US bank regulator faults several large lenders over debanking practices
item.description: A top US bank regulator issued a report on Wednesday finding some of the country's largest banks unfairly denied services to some clients on political, religious or other grounds, but stopped short of imposing penalties.
item.dc:creator: Pete Schroeder, Manya Saini
item.content:encoded: A top US bank regulator issued a report on Wednesday finding some of the country's largest banks unfairly denied services to some clients on political, religious or other grounds, but stopped short of imposing penalties. The [USN:L4N4491DY TEXT:"debanking"] report from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency covered nine of the nation's largest banks by asset size. The regulator found each had policies restricting some clients' access to financial services based on subjective criteria rather than financial risk. Banks have said they close accounts or deny services because of legal, financial or reputational risks, not politics. The regulator criticized the banks for the practices, but did not indicate any sanctions or punishments were forthcoming. It said it may consider policy changes to discourage such activity. FAIR ACCESS IS A MANDATE: REGULATOR The review, which began in September 2025, scrutinized banks that collectively hold a majority of US commercial banking assets. "Americans should have access to financial services regardless of their beliefs, affiliations, or political views. Fair access to financial services is not a mantra — it is a mandate," Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan Gould said in a statement. After President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing a review of alleged debanking, [USN:L4N42C182 TEXT:"regulators and banks moved to eliminate the use of reputation risk "]in assessing clients, though[USN:L4N4491DY TEXT:" the issue remains contentious. "] Conservative politicians and business groups have accused banks of cutting off companies in sectors including fossil fuels, firearms and cryptocurrency , making debanking a flashpoint in Washington financial policy. Large banks have denied rejecting customers on political or religious grounds, arguing instead that years of aggressive regulatory pressure discouraged them from serving certain sectors and urging Washington to establish clearer rules on who they can and cannot serve. The OCC found that concerns about public opinion had led at least one bank to distance itself from certain customer affiliations that could be viewed as partisan. It added that banks generally lacked clear, measurable standards and objective, risk-based criteria for assessing reputational risks associated with customer relationships. "The OCC will continue to work with our regulatory partners to further assess the extent to which bank policies implementing money laundering and terrorist financing program requirements have contributed to debanking and will take appropriate action as needed," the report said. Earlier this year, Trump [USN:L4N3YN1QS TEXT:"filed a $5 billion lawsuit"] against JPMorgan Chase and its CEO Jamie Dimon, alleging the bank closed several of his accounts for political reasons. JPMorgan, the largest US bank, has denied closing accounts on political or religious grounds, and filed a motion to dismiss the lawsuit on Tuesday. A bank spokesperson said the lender prohibits political and religious discrimination, and added, "Years of operating in a regulatory environment that often second-guessed decisions contributed to a culture of caution across the banking industry. That system needs fixing." Trump has also [USN:S0N3OG012 TEXT:"accused other lenders"], including Bank of America (BAC.N) , the country's second-biggest lender by assets, of debanking him in early 2025. A Bank of America spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the new report. The bank has previously said it does not comment on client matters and would welcome clearer rules from bank regulators on how to conduct its activities.

item.description: BANGKOK, Oct 14 : Thailand's return to economic growth of about 3 per cent is "definitely possible" within three years if it can tackle some of its structural issues, a deputy central bank governor said on Wednesday, signalling alignment with the government's stance.The Bank of Thailand's monetary policy will

Thailand can return to 3% growth within 2-3 years, central bank official says

Bank of Thailand Deputy Governor Piti Disyatat speaks during an interview with Reuters, in Bangkok, Thailand, May 2, 2025. REUTERS/Orathai Sriring

FAST

BANGKOK, Oct 14 : Thailand's return to economic growth of about 3 per cent is "definitely possible" within three years if it can tackle some of its structural issues, a deputy central bank governor said on Wednesday, signalling alignment with the government's stance. The Bank of Thailand's monetary policy will remain accommodative for now and the policy rate, currently at 1.00 per cent, will normalise only when the economy is ready, Piti Disyatat, the deputy governor for monetary stability, told Reuters.  Piti said he expects the economy to grow 2.3 per cent or slightly higher this year and to expand by 1.8 per cent in 2027. The central bank's baseline scenario is to get back to a 2.8 per cent to 3 per cent range the year after.    "In the more distant future, two or three years horizon, we do think our potential trend growth is around 2.8 per cent to 3 per cent. So it is definitely possible to grow to 3 per cent and we expect growth to get to that level," he said in an interview on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund-World Bank annual meetings.

"It's subject to not having negative shocks and also partly subject to some of the constraints that are within our control, the so-called more structural things that can be alleviated." Backed by a government push for new investments in key sectors such as semiconductors and data centres, Thailand's economy is expected to grow by 2.5 per cent next year and potentially by 3 per cent within the next three years, Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas told Reuters last month. In an interview last month, Don Nakornthab, Bank of Thailand assistant governor for monetary policy, said the Thai economy's potential growth rate stood at 2.7 per cent, which would take four to five years to reach. RATE CUT 'HARD TO IMAGINE' Southeast Asia's second-largest economy has struggled in recent years compared to other countries in the region, weighed down by weak demand and stubbornly high levels of household debt. The economy expanded 1.9 per cent annually in the second quarter of 2026, down sharply from 2.8 per cent in the previous quarter. The central bank left its key interest rate unchanged at 1.00 per cent in August and cut its policy rate six times between October 2024 and February, amounting to a total of 150 basis points, as it sought to give a boost to the economy. It will next review policy on October 28. "We don't foresee any reductions in rates," Piti said. "It's hard to imagine a cut unless there's a big shock hit, because 1 per cent is low historically. We've never been at 1 per cent outside of crisis times."  He added: "Definitely, I think at some point we will have to normalise interest rates when the economy is ready."

Source: Reuters
